thread:
jordan: Heads-up — I'm proposing a short validation sweep next week to reduce Xid/ECC noise after the 545.23 driver push. Goal: cut transient Xid spikes by ~50% and validate drain/replace heuristics.

maya: +1. what are the failure signals we'll accept as success?

jordan: Plan: 1) run synthetic long-seq transformer inference for 12h per AZ, 2) enable enhanced ECC sampling on suspect cards, 3) correlate Xid counts with pcie resets and kernel logs. Success = 50% drop in 95p Xid rate vs baseline and no >2% QoS latency regressions.

liam: How do we run the synthetic load — existing smoke harness or new script?

jordan: New harness (lightweight) — "gpu-sweep". Example:
```
./gpu-sweep --model gpt-medium --seq 4096 --batch 1 --duration 12h --kvcache-warmup 30m
```
It pins to a single GPU and captures dmesg + nvidia-smi logs.

samira: Can we reuse the drain automation? I want to validate node-level drain + auto-replace flow so we don't manual-intervene mid-sweep.

jordan: Yes — we'll use the staged-drain policy: mark node.sweep=true, wait for 2x grace windows, then auto-evict pods and kick a replace job. If Xid count > threshold during sweep, node goes into quarantine.

maya: Threshold numbers?

jordan: Threshold: >10 Xid-13 spikes in 1h OR any ECC single-event >5 in 1h. We also consider PCIe resets: any soft-reset followed by >3 Xid in 30m triggers quarantine.

liam: Who's owning the dashboard/alerts? We need a one-page view showing per-GPU Xid rate, ECC rate, recent kernel OOPS, and last drain action.

samira: I'll own the dashboard. I'll add a new panel in infra-gpu with these queries and a reconciliation view to map GPU IDs -> host.

deploy-bot: Canary pipeline queued: sweeps/driver-545.23/region-sweep-1. Estimated time 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC.

oncall-bot: Incident stub created: #INC-2026-1124-driver-sweep-candidate. Use this to post triage notes.

maya: Cost note — running 12h per AZ on reserved GPUs adds ~120 GPU-hours. Suggest we prioritize regions with historically higher Xid density first.

jordan: Good point. Sweep order: us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 -> ap-northeast-1. We'll stop the sweep early if Xid reduction is <20% after the first region.

liam: Any rollback plan if we see perf regressions?

jordan: Hot rollback: taint nodes, fail-over workloads to Dedicated pool, then revert the driver via our OS hotpatch (tested last month). Worst-case: full node reprovision and reimage.

samira: I'll add a per-region watch channel and a quick-runbook with CLI snippets for rollback. Example commands I'll include:
```
# mark node for quarantine
infractl node annotate host-123 sweep=quarantine
# revert driver
infractl host upgrade --image driver-legacy-543.11 --force
```

maya: LGTM. Let's sync in the weekly infra ops meeting Thursday and finalize the sweep window.

jordan: Thanks — I'll circulate the runbook + schedule invite. Short updates in this thread only. :thumbsup:
